topic: Tetravalence of Carbon and Shapes of Organic Compounds
title: Carbon Shapes sp3 sp2 sp Explained Simply | PUC Chemistry Class 11
description:
A ceiling fan is flat, a seesaw is a straight line, and a sea wall block points four ways. Carbon makes all three shapes. In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Chemistry (NCERT Chapter 8, Organic Chemistry: Some Basic Principles and Techniques) we learn why carbon is tetravalent and how its bonds set the shape of organic compounds.

On the molecule bench, carbon pairs its four outer electrons into four bonds, mixes its orbitals into sp3 (109.5°, methane), sp2 (120°, ethene) and sp (180°, ethyne), and we see why more s character means shorter, stronger bonds: C-C 154 pm, C=C 134 pm, C≡C 120 pm. Then the pi bond: sideways overlap, no rotation, and why it is the most reactive spot. A full worked example counts sigma and pi bonds, then the exam trap, an original JEE / NEET pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

This is Episode 78 of our PUC Chemistry series.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, NEET and JEE Main students. For NCERT, CBSE, ICSE/ISC, PUC, NEET and JEE students.

In this video:
0:00 Three shapes, one atom
0:29 Chapter 8: why carbon makes four bonds
1:05 The molecule bench: sp3 tetrahedral
1:35 sp2 and sp: double and triple bonds
2:11 s character, bond length and strength, link by link
2:54 Pi bonds: no rotation, most reactive
3:48 Worked example: sigma, pi and hybridisation
4:29 Exam trap: is a double bond twice as strong?
4:54 Practice question (JEE / NEET pattern)
5:30 Recap and three questions to answer

Next episode: Structural Representations of Organic Compounds. How do chemists draw a big molecule with one zigzag line?
